meta.tagline: Hawker tables, supertrees and three cuisines in a garden city

pills: Hawker culture on the UNESCO list
Home of the world's best airport

overview.title: Welcome to Singapore
overview.intro: Singapore is proof of how ambitious a city-state can be: giant supertrees rise between the towers, a waterfall pours inside the airport, and the streets are operating-theatre clean. But beneath the polished surface simmers the real treasure — at the steaming stalls of the hawker centres, Chinese, Malay and Indian cooking have simmered shoulder to shoulder for a century. Step out of the air-conditioned mall and onto a plastic stool: Singapore's heart beats there, over a plate of char kway teow.

local_word.definition: Singlish's best-loved word: 'fantastic, pure pleasure'. It escapes you unbidden after the first spoon of laksa — and if it doesn't, you're at the wrong stall.

rules.title: The rules are real, and so are the fines
rules.description: Gum sales banned, no eating on the metro, serious fines for littering: this city protects its order with rules. There's tolerance for visitors, but don't test the line — the rules work the same for everyone.

rules.title: Learn the chope culture
rules.description: A tissue packet left on a hawker table means 'this seat is taken': the system is called chope, and it is sacred. Chope your own table first, then join the stall queue — that's the local order of operations.

rules.title: Manage your layers between street and aircon
rules.description: Outside is 30 degrees and humid all year; inside is icy air-conditioning: light clothes + a thin extra layer is the city uniform. Plan walks for morning and evening, malls and museums for midday.

quick_facts.label: Airport
quick_facts.sub: MRT to centre ~40 min · the Jewel waterfall inside

quick_facts.label: Getting around
quick_facts.sub: Tap straight in with a contactless card

tip.label: The Singapore philosophy
tip.text: In this city the distance between luxury and street is one doorway: leave the Marina Bay rooftop bar and sit on a hawker stool ten minutes later. Fitting both into one evening is the shortest way to understand Singapore.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: Singapore's transport is a machine that runs without friction: the MRT goes everywhere, a contactless card opens every gate, and the ride app waits in reserve.

items.title: Changi to the centre
items.description: The MRT's green-blue combination reaches the centre in 40 minutes; a taxi takes 25 at a reasonable metered fare. If your flight is early or late, give the Jewel waterfall an hour — this airport is a sight in itself.

items.title: The MRT — cold, fast, flawless
items.description: The metro web covers the island: tap through with a contactless bank card and the daily cap calculates itself. Take the no-eating rule seriously — and enjoy the air-conditioning.

items.title: The double-decker buses
items.description: The bus network opens the neighbourhoods the MRT misses: the top-deck front seat is the air-conditioned way to learn the city. The same card works — remember to tap off as well.

items.title: Walking — a morning and evening affair
items.description: Marina Bay, the river and the neighbourhood cores are walkable, but budget for the humidity. Use the shaded routes and air-conditioned shopping links as corridors — the locals do.

items.title: Taxis and the apps
items.description: Taxis are metered and honest; the apps (Grab) show the fare upfront. Peak and night surcharges are normal — not a surprise, a tariff.

callout.label: Card tip
callout.text: You don't need a separate transit card: your contactless bank card taps straight through on MRT and bus. One rule — use the same card in and out; the system adds up the day and charges the cheapest cap.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Singapore choosing a neighbourhood is choosing a theme: the bay skyline, Chinatown's shophouses, Arab Street's colours or Katong's Peranakan façades.

local_word.definition: The traditional coffee shop: the kopi ordering language is a dictionary in itself — kopi-o is black with sugar, kopi-c with evaporated milk, kopi kosong unsweetened. The morning trio of soft eggs + kaya toast + kopi is the national breakfast.

items.name: Marina Bay and the Civic District
items.description: The bay skyline, museums and light shows at your door: Singapore's showcase face. High prices, flawless views and location — the showy base for a first visit.

items.name: Chinatown and Tanjong Pagar
items.description: Shophouse façades, temples and hawker centres interlocked, with night bars and boutique hotels on the same streets. The natural centre of a food-first visit.

items.name: Kampong Glam and Arab Street
items.description: Fabric shops, cafés and murals around the Sultan Mosque: Haji Lane's boutiques are the young crowd's route. Characterful small hotels — for those after colour and rhythm.

items.name: Little India
items.description: Spice scent, garland stalls and Mustafa, the 24-hour shopping legend: the friendliest prices in town. Dense, noisy and utterly alive — Singapore unfiltered.

items.name: Katong and Joo Chiat
items.description: Pastel Peranakan façades, laksa stalls and walking distance to the shore: graceful neighbourhood life off the tourist route. A quarter hour to the centre by MRT.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: On the equator there are no seasons, only rhythm: 30 degrees all year, sudden downpours and a festival calendar — plan by the events, not the rain.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Festival Spring
items.subtitle: February-April · New Year afterglow, the drier stretch
items.description: The year's relatively dry slice: Chinese New Year colours February, and April passes comfortably for hawker crawls. The humidity is its usual self — the early-morning plan remains the golden rule.

callout.label: February tip
callout.text: If you're here around Chinese New Year, walk Chinatown's lights and market in the evening; know that some hawker stalls close for the first two festival days — build your plan across neighbourhoods.

items.label: Summer
items.name: The Hot Routine
items.subtitle: May-August · Standard tropics: heat + afternoon downpour
items.description: The equatorial routine runs in full: morning sun, a short violent afternoon shower, a warm evening. June-July's Great Singapore Sale calls the shoppers, July's food festival the flavour hunters.

callout.label: Downpour tip
callout.text: A rain radar app is Singapore's secret weapon: the downpours usually last 30-60 minutes. When the rain starts, sit in a kopitiam, order kopi, wait — the city was built to this rhythm.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Lights and Race Season
items.subtitle: September-November · The F1 night race, Deepavali lights
items.description: In September the Formula 1 night race pulls the city inside the circuit — hotels peak that week. In October-November Deepavali turns Little India into a sea of light. The rains build with November.

callout.label: F1 note
callout.text: In race week the Marina roads close and hotel prices multiply: shift the week if you're not watching; if you are, lock tickets and lodging months ahead.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Monsoon and Sparkle
items.subtitle: December-January · The wet stretch, festive lights
items.description: The northeast monsoon brings the wettest slice, but the city is built for it: Orchard Road dresses in lights, and the covered walkways and malls make the rain unfelt. In the rain's pauses the gardens are washed and cool.

callout.label: December tip
callout.text: The rainy-December evening formula: the Jewel waterfall + the National Gallery + the Marina walkways to the light show — a complete Singapore day with the umbrella barely opened.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Singapore's true monuments are its hawker centres: in these UNESCO-listed open kitchens, the masters of three cultures cook under one roof.

local_word.definition: Malay for 'to eat': in Singlish it is verb, invitation and way of life. 'Makan already?' (have you eaten?) is this city's warm way of asking how you are — and the answer always comes with a stall recommendation.

items.name: Hainanese chicken rice — the national plate
items.description: Silken poached chicken, rice cooked in chicken fat, ginger and chilli sauce: simplicity's summit. Every Singaporean has a sworn stall — join the one with the queue.
items.tag: National classic · with the chilli sauce

items.name: Laksa and char kway teow
items.description: Coconut-spiced laksa soup and wok-smoky char kway teow noodles: two heavyweights, two different stalls. Katong laksa is eaten with a spoon only — the noodles come pre-cut.

items.name: Chilli crab — the shell feast
items.description: Crab in sweet-hot tomato sauce with mantou buns for dunking: Singapore's celebration plate. Eaten by hand, apron on, billed by weight — ask the price first.

items.name: Kaya toast + soft eggs + kopi
items.description: Toast with coconut kaya jam, half-boiled eggs with soy sauce, and kopi whose ordering language is an art of its own: the kopitiam breakfast's holy trio.

items.name: Satay and the night stalls
items.description: Marinated skewers over coals, peanut sauce and cucumber-onion garnish: ordered by the dozen in the evening satay streets. Iced sugarcane juice alongside — the night classic.

items.name: Ais kacang and tropical sweets
items.description: Shaved ice under coloured syrups, red beans and corn: the official cure for tropical heat. Mango sticky rice and the durian courage test play in the same sweet league.
items.tag: The cooling sweet · the brave try durian

callout.label: The hawker rule
callout.text: Three signs never lie at a hawker centre: a long queue, a stall mastering one single dish, and an old newspaper clipping on the wall. Return your own tray — it's the rule now, with a fine behind it. And don't forget to chope with a tissue packet.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the supertrees; these six are the garden city's hidden layers.

items.name: The Southern Ridges walk
items.description: From the rippling wooden bridge of Henderson Waves onto forest-crest walkways: you cross the city's south at canopy level. Start early — the macaques and birds wake before you.

items.name: Pulau Ubin
items.description: Ten minutes by boat from Changi jetty into 1960s Singapore: village houses, dirt tracks and the Chek Jawa wetlands. Rent a bike — the island is the wild sibling the city-state kept.

items.name: The MacRitchie TreeTop Walk
items.description: The rainforest reserve's suspension bridge crosses above the canopy: monkey families, monitor lizards and silence. The full loop takes three hours — carry water, walk in the morning cool.

items.name: Tiong Bahru
items.description: A market, independent bookshops and one of the city's oldest hawker centres among 1930s art deco blocks: chwee kueh (steamed rice cakes) is the morning classic. An elegance not yet fully on the tourist route.

items.name: The Botanic Gardens at 7 am
items.description: The UNESCO gardens are famous for the orchids, but the real magic is at 7 am: tai chi groups, rain-tree shade and nearly empty paths. Entry free — Singapore's most generous gift.

items.name: Sentosa's quiet end — Tanjong Beach
items.description: Step away from Sentosa's theme-park face: Tanjong beach at the southern tip is nearly empty on weekdays. Palm shade, warm water and a ship-silhouetted sunset — the island's calm face.

callout.label: Garden tip
callout.text: The Gardens by the Bay conservatories (Cloud Forest + Flower Dome) are the best midday-heat refuge, and the supertree light show (Garden Rhapsody) runs two free sessions each evening. Order accordingly: conservatories at noon, lights at night — a bay walk in between.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Singapore plays in honesty's world league; its traps are not scams but price and planning mistakes.

items.name: The rooftop bar price shock
items.description: One cocktail at a skyline rooftop costs four hawker meals; add service and tax and the bill multiplies.
items.instead: Plan the rooftop as a one-drink view break and move the rest of the evening to hawkers and neighbourhood bars. Some viewpoints charge entry with a drink voucher — do the maths first.

items.name: Buying everything at Sentosa
items.description: The island's amusements bought one by one melt a wallet, and the 'all-inclusive' bundles swell with activities you'll never use.
items.instead: Enter Sentosa by the free Boardwalk and cut the plan to two or three picks: the beach is free anyway, and so is the sunset. Buy classics like the luge at the early online price.

items.name: The alcohol clock and price surprise
items.description: Alcohol tax is high and shop sales stop after 10.30 pm: whoever doesn't know loses both budget and evening.
items.instead: Shop for drinks in daylight and chase the bars' happy hours (usually 5-8 pm). Hawker beer costs half the restaurant price — the stall beer is a legitimate classic.

items.name: The 'tax-free electronics' haggle
items.description: In some tourist electronics arcades the game of unlabelled prices, missing receipts and 'today only' discounts still lives.
items.instead: Buy electronics from chain stores and compare prices online. Process the tourist GST refund yourself at the airport with official receipts — no middleman needed.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Singapore's budget balance is one sentence: eat at hawkers, spend on experiences. What three hawker meals a day save funds a conservatory ticket + one rooftop cocktail + a night safari with ease.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A full dose of Singapore, from kopitiam to supertrees

steps.title: A kopitiam breakfast
steps.description: Kaya toast + soft eggs + kopi: try the ordering language, and smile if you get it wrong — they'll fix it. Start the day the local way.

steps.title: Chinatown and the temples
steps.description: Shophouse façades, the Buddha Tooth Relic temple and Sri Mariamman's painted gopuram: three cultures in one quarter.

steps.title: The hawker lunch summit
steps.description: A chicken rice + laksa tour at Maxwell or a neighbourhood hawker: chope with a tissue packet, pick the queued stall, prepare to say 'shiok'.

steps.title: A cool break in the conservatories
steps.description: Cloud Forest's indoor waterfall and the Flower Dome: the midday heat's most graceful refuge. A bay walk on the way out.

steps.title: The Marina skyline and one cocktail
steps.description: A one-drink view break at a rooftop bar: watch the skyline light up over the bay — with one drink, the bill stays elegant.

steps.title: Garden Rhapsody + a night makan tour
steps.description: Watch the supertrees' free light show from the ground; then a dozen skewers + sugarcane juice on a satay street: the night closes with makan.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: City, neighbourhoods and the wild side

steps.title: Classic Singapore
steps.description: The one-day flow above: kopitiam, Chinatown, hawker, conservatories, light show.

steps.title: The neighbourhood tour
steps.description: Kampong Glam in the morning (Sultan Mosque + Haji Lane), a banana-leaf thali in Little India at noon; Katong's Peranakan façades + laksa in the afternoon; riverside dinner and the Civic District lights at night.

steps.title: Green and wild Singapore
steps.description: The MacRitchie treetop walk or a Pulau Ubin bike morning; the Botanic Gardens + a Tiong Bahru pause in the afternoon; the Night Safari or a Tanjong Beach sunset in the evening — let the farewell be tropical.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: English is official in Singapore, but Singlish is the city's real music: these five suit both your ear and your tongue.

items.meaning: The sentence-ending emphasis: 'Can lah!' (of course it works!) — Singlish's signature
'Fantastic, pure pleasure' — arrives unbidden after the first spoon of laksa
Food / to eat — 'go makan?' is this city's warmest invitation
To reserve a table with a tissue packet — the hawker order's sacred verb
'Sure, it works!' — Singaporean practicality in one word; 'can can' is even more positive
